issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a parameterless Rideable.messageOnRide() method (returns a String), but the solution implements Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and corresponding implementations in Pig and Seal also require a String parameter. This mismatch between the intended interface (no parameters) and the solution (with a parameter) is structural: students following the problem description or the template Main will implement/expect messageOnRide() with no arguments, while the solution's types use a different signature, causing compilation/signature confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signatures consistent. Either: (A) change the solution's Rideable and its implementations (Pig, Seal) to define messageOnRide() with no parameters and return the string as specified by the problem (e.g., "Riding on Pig Doodle"), or (B) update the problem statement and template to require messageOnRide(String equipment) and adjust the examples accordingly. Option A is recommended to match the current problem description and template usage.

issues.description: The Rideable interface's method signature differs across artifacts: the problem statement UML and the template Main expect a no-argument method messageOnRide():String, but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and the implementing classes (Pig, Seal) also use that single-parameter signature. This mismatch (no-arg vs. one-arg) breaks the direct mapping students must make from the exercise description to the provided template and to the reference solution and will cause calls like r.messageOnRide() in the template Main to fail against the solution API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's Rideable and its implementations to declare messageOnRide() with no parameters (matching the UML and template Main), or (B) update the problem statement UML and template code to require messageOnRide(String equipment) and adapt examples accordingly. Prefer (A) if the original exercise intention was a no-argument messageOnRide().
